extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, disciplinary counsel, and administrative adjudicators
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural rules governing service, default, liability, and sanctions in USPTO disciplinary proceedings under 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. Parts 10 and 11. Includes service methods, default consequences, substantive misconduct rules, fee/payment obligations, statute of limitations, and penalty factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized methods of service (37 C.F.R. § 11.35(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A complaint may be served on a respondent by personal delivery, by mailing a copy by 'Express Mail,' first-class mail, or any delivery service that provides the ability to confirm delivery or attempted delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If these methods fail, service by publication (Official Gazette) for two consecutive weeks may be used (see § 11.35(b)). The page documents an attempted certified-mail service (returned/unclaimed) followed by service by publication, which was held to be appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service by publication (37 C.F.R. § 11.35(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a copy of the complaint cannot be delivered through the §11.35(a) procedures, the OED Director shall serve the respondent by causing an appropriate notice to be published in the Official Gazette for two consecutive weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time for filing an answer is thirty days from the second publication of the notice. Failure to timely file an answer after publication may constitute admission of the allegations and permit entry of an initial decision on default.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time to answer and default consequences (37 C.F.R. § 11.36(a),(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: An answer to a complaint must be filed within the time set (but no less than 30 days from the date the complaint is filed). Failure to timely file an answer constitutes an admission of the allegations and may result in entry of default judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default may be entered without a separate motion; a respondent who does not answer is deemed to have admitted the complaint's allegations. The page applies the 30-day rule (complaint filed January 7; answer due by February 8) and finds respondent in default for non-response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of motions and completion of mail service (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.42(b)(2),(f); § 11.43)
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions may be served by first-class mail, 'Express Mail,' or other delivery service; service by mail is completed when the paper mailed in the United States is placed into custody of the U.S. Postal Service. The hearing officer determines time periods for filing responses to motions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In a default context where respondent has not appeared, it is not necessary to allow an extended period to respond to a motion for default, though the hearing officer may set time under §11.43. The Motion in this case was served by certified mail and no reply was received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on conduct prejudicial to administration of justice (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not 'engage in conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issuance or submission of bad/dishonored checks to the PTO (and failure to 'make good' after notice) is treated as conduct prejudicial to administration of justice. The decision cites multiple disciplinary precedents finding bad checks evidence professional misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent fee/payment timing and methods (35 U.S.C. § 151; 37 C.F.R. § 1.22(a); § 1.23)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent fees and charges payable to the USPTO are required to be paid in advance, i.e., at the time of requesting any action for which a fee is payable. Payments may be made by check, cashier's check, money order, or credit card per §1.23.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. §151 requires payment of an issue fee within three months of notice or the application is regarded as abandoned and the patent will not issue or will lapse. Failure to timely pay issue fees can create adverse consequences for clients and the enforceability of patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to 'make good' on returned checks and pay processing fees
rubrics_metrics.description: When a check submitted to the USPTO is returned (dishonored), the practitioner is expected to 'make good' on the check (provide necessary funds) and pay the PTO's returned-check processing fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to remedy returned checks despite written notifications is an aggravating factor and supports finding willfulness and professional misconduct; PTO relied on multiple written notices not acted upon by respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statute of limitations for disciplinary enforcement (28 U.S.C. § 2462)
rubrics_metrics.description: A five-year federal statute of limitations applies to actions enforcing civil fines or penalties; an action must be commenced within five years from when the claim first accrued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A claim accrues when factual and legal prerequisites for filing suit are in place. The decision finds one alleged dishonored check from July 2002 time-barred while later checks were within the five-year period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalty determination factors (37 C.F.R. § 11.54(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining any penalty, consider: (1) whether practitioner violated a duty owed to a client/public/legal system/profession; (2) whether conduct was intentional, knowing, or negligent; (3) the amount of actual or potential injury caused; and (4) existence of aggravating or mitigating factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These four factors are used to calibrate sanctions (e.g., suspension length). The decision applied them, finding duty violations, willfulness based on notice and inaction, actual/potential injury (possible abandonment/unenforceability of patents), an aggravating refusal to remediate, and mitigating long practice/respectively limited incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of competent representation (37 C.F.R. § 10.77 — referenced)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners owe clients a duty to represent their interests competently (as prescribed in 37 C.F.R. § 10.77).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failing to ensure required PTO fees are paid can breach that duty by risking clients' intellectual property rights (abandonment, unenforceability). The decision cites this duty in assessing harm to clients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of precedent and ABA Standards when assessing sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparative disciplinary authority decisions and the American Bar Association Standards for Imposing Lawyer Sanctions are used to inform appropriate sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision compares respondent's conduct to prior cases (Adams, Anger, Lococo) and cites ABA Standard 9.22(j) and other authorities to place the sanction on an appropriate point in the range (here concluding a 120-day suspension).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures and timelines for appeal, suspension responsibilities, and reinstatement (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.55, 11.58, 11.59(a), 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any appeal from an Initial Decision must be filed with the USPTO within 30 days and must include exceptions and supporting reasons. Rules also prescribe practitioner responsibilities during suspension and procedures for petitioning for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no timely appeal is filed, the Initial Decision becomes final and effective 30 days after issuance. Decisions are published (OED Reading Room) and the respondent's obligations during suspension and pathways to reinstatement are governed by cited sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice of disciplinary decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary findings and suspensions are published in the Office's official publications and posted in the OED Reading Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice of Suspension is to be published; the decision includes a sample Notice of Suspension and identifies the public posting location (OED Reading Room URL). Publication serves as public notice and part of the sanction's implementation.
